html:
Queen of the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth realms from 1952 to 2022. Her reign of seventy years is the longest in British history.

She was not born to be queen. Her uncle Edward VIII gave up the throne in 1936, and her father became George VI. During the Second World War she trained as a mechanic and driver in the army. She married Philip Mountbatten in 1947 and became queen at 25, when her father died in February 1952. Her coronation in 1953 was one of the first great events watched on television.

Her reign saw the end of most of the British Empire, as colony after colony became independent in the age of decolonisation. She put much effort into the Commonwealth, the association of former colonies, as its head. Fifteen prime ministers served under her in Britain, from Winston Churchill to Liz Truss.

She stayed above party politics and rarely gave her views in public, which helped keep the monarchy popular through family scandals. She died at Balmoral in September 2022, and her son became Charles III.
sum: Queen of the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth realms from 1952 to 2022. Her reign of seventy years is the longest in British history.
